1000243.etyen:
Borrowed from English Saturn (“former American automobile marque”). The English brand name originated as the name of a General Motors project in 1982 and was retained when Saturn Corporation was formally established in 1985.
The project was named after the Saturn V rocket, which had carried the Apollo missions to the Moon. The name was intended to evoke the technological ambition and success of the American space program at a time when General Motors was seeking to compete more effectively with Japanese automobile manufacturers.
The rocket's name ultimately derives from the same astronomical n

1005107.etyen:
Compound of forsvinning (“disappearance, vanishing”) + punkt (“point”), literally “disappearance point”.
The first element forsvinning (“disappearance, vanishing”) is formed from forsvinne (“to disappear, vanish”) with -ing (“action/result-forming noun suffix”). The verb derives from Middle Low German vorswinden (“to disappear, vanish”), whose prefix vor- (“verbal prefix denoting, among other things, loss or a negative result”) continues Proto-West Germanic *fra- (“verbal prefix meaning away, off”), while its second element is cognate with svinne (“to dwindle, fade”), ultimately from Proto-Ger
